gaps.sentence: I will tell her the news when I ___ her at the party.
gaps.hint: when clauses take present for future
gaps.explanation: Time clauses with future meaning use the present simple, not 'will': see.

gaps.sentence: If the hotel ___ a pool, we would book it for the whole team.
gaps.hint: unreal present lack of a facility
gaps.explanation: The hotel does not have a pool now, so the if-clause takes the past simple: had.

gaps.sentence: Unless the tickets ___ within a week, ask for a refund.
gaps.hint: unless plus present before an imperative
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' clauses take the present simple, even before an imperative result: arrive.

gaps.sentence: If we ___ tickets today, they will cost half the price.
gaps.explanation: The condition is present simple; only the result clause uses 'will': book.

gaps.sentence: If the alarm sounds, ___ the building immediately.
gaps.hint: an instruction after if, imperative result
gaps.explanation: Instructions after 'if' keep the present simple in the if-clause and use the imperative as the result: leave.

gaps.sentence: If I ___ a million euros, I would travel the world for a year.
gaps.explanation: Second conditionals use the past simple after 'if' for unreal presents: won.

gaps.sentence: I wish I ___ to your advice — then I would not be in this mess.
gaps.hint: regret about the past, past perfect
gaps.explanation: 'Wish' plus the past perfect expresses regret about the past: had listened.

gaps.sentence: If only I ___ more at university!
gaps.explanation: 'If only + past perfect' — regret about a past failure.
